A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PROPS by Corrado and Hanna. The complete 26-page v2 and 27-page v3, including their appendices, equations, figures, and tables, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original GridWorld, MuJoCo, and discrete-action experiments, including learning performance, sampling error, ablations, and runtimes.

after.justification: Section 6 and the appendices report original GridWorld and MuJoCo results, including oracle comparisons, sampling-error analyses, ablations, runtimes, and hyperparameter robustness.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same sampling and target-update procedure, behavior-policy reset, clipped objective, KL regularization, and stopping rule. Oldest-batch exclusion and policy classes are unchanged between v2 Appendix B and v3 Appendix C. Expanded ROS explanations and the new theoretical distributions do not establish a change to the implemented PROPS method.

E1.justification: The CartPole-v1, LunarLander-v2, and Discrete2D100-v0 experiments in v2 Appendix D.4 are absent from v3. This removes the continuous-state, discrete-action evaluation suite. GridWorld, all six MuJoCo tasks, and evaluation with both random and expert fixed policies remain.

E2.justification: V3 adds an oracle to GridWorld Figure 2 and ROS to the fixed-policy ablation, removes PPO from the buffer-size comparison, and includes PPO/PPO-Buffer in the revised sensitivity comparison. Its bias/variance figure also replaces the ROS legend entry with Oracle Adaptive Sampling, although the prose still names ROS. The principal learning baselines remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Return curves switch from interquartile means to ordinary means, and v3 introduces cross-task normalized aggregation. Fixed-policy tuning now fixes regularization at 0.1 and KL cutoff at 0.03; the RL sweep removes update frequencies 2048/4096 and regularization 0.01. Bias/variance plots extend from 2,000 to 10,000 samples. Some settings remain ambiguous: Figure 11 says random policy while its discussion says expert, and Figure 5's normalization formula conflicts with its higher-is-better interpretation.

E4.justification: V3 replaces v2 Figure 19's individual hyperparameter curves on three tasks with tuned-versus-pooled performance and performance profiles across six MuJoCo tasks in Appendix G. It also revises bias/variance and fixed-policy ablation analyses and removes the discrete-task comparisons with and without historic data. The clipping, regularization, and larger-buffer ablation questions are retained.

E5.justification: V3 adds paired t-tests at the 95% confidence level for Table 1. Captions report 50 rather than 10 seeds for fixed-policy GridWorld and 10 rather than 5 for fixed-policy ablations. These are changes in reported run counts; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun. Existing bootstrap intervals and three-run runtime standard errors remain.

E6.justification: V3 adds checkpoint return entries, oracle results, and aggregated performance, replaces several sampling-error and return curves, and removes the three discrete-action result sets. Table 1 newly reports final Ant-v4 means of 4930 for PROPS, 4741 for PPO-Buffer, and 5014 for PPO, retaining PPO's slight advantage. Changed metrics and settings prevent interpreting revised curves as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: New Appendix B Propositions 3–4 derive corrective sampling distributions and feasibility conditions relating historic and additional data. V3 also changes the formal objective to an infinite horizon, corrects the opposite-gradient relation in Section 4's example, and explicitly includes irreducibility in the appendix proposition. The original state-visitation convergence argument is retained.

C1.justification: The central claims that PROPS reduces sampling error and improves data efficiency remain. V3 drops v2's broad conceptual contribution and concluding maxim that on-policy learning requires on-policy data rather than on-policy sampling, framing the contributions more narrowly around empirical sampling-error reduction and learning efficiency.

C2.justification: V3 newly explains that historic advantage estimates remain biased after correcting the state-action distribution and suggests reducing GAE lambda as a possible mitigation. It discusses undiscounted-gradient bias and explicitly limits the convergence theory to tabular settings. It also adds an early-error-reduction explanation for HalfCheetah; the general HalfCheetah exception was already discussed in v2 Appendix D.3.

D1.justification: V3 Table 4 newly discloses selected hyperparameters for each MuJoCo task, and the documented search ranges change. Conversely, v2's half-budget buffer specification for fixed-policy experiments and uniform-policy setup for the bias/variance analysis are omitted. Core implementation details, network sizes, hardware, and evaluation settings remain documented.

R1.justification: V3 adds Liu et al. (2024), Papini et al. (2024), Nota and Thomas (2019), and Patterson et al. (2023), expanding discussion of importance-sampling approaches, gradient bias, and evaluation design. Achiam, Silver, and Kakade–Langford references are removed. The overall positioning relative to exploration, policy evaluation, importance weighting, and data reuse remains similar.

P1.justification: The introduction and ROS explanation are substantially rewritten. Section 5 gains separate ROS and PROPS subsections, sampling-error estimation moves from v2 Appendix C into v3 Section 6.1, related work and discussion gain topic headings, and the appendices are reorganized. These changes substantially revise the narrative beyond adding scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, the gradient example is boxed, and sampling-error plots are moved and expanded within the main text. V3 adds checkpoint and selected-hyperparameter tables plus aggregate plots, replaces the sensitivity display, and removes discrete-action figures. Axes, legends, figure arrangements, typography, and the publication layout change extensively.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects the gradient-example sign, discloses selected settings, and makes important advantage-bias and convergence limitations explicit. Its checkpoint table and statistical tests also make the central comparisons easier to assess. These gains are partly offset by removing three discrete-action benchmarks and introducing inconsistencies in normalization, fixed-policy labels, and the bias/variance comparator description. The net improvement is therefore limited.
